title.narrative: Integrated Humanitarian Support for Safe and Dignified Return: Enhancing Health, Nutrition, WASH, and Livelihoods for Returnees and Host Communities in Aleppo and Hama

description.narrative: ltpgtThe 12-month project addresses critical needs in Aleppo and Hama governorates by increasing access to essential health, nutrition, WASH, and food security services for 88,660 crisis-affected people. Under envelopes 1 and 2, ACF will implement a multi-sectoral and integrated response targeting Jebel Samaan Sub-district in Aleppo and Karnaz Sub-district in Hama. The intervention is rooted in ACF-led multisectoral assessments and is designed in close coordination with local authorities, sector leads, and the Directorates of Health (DoH) and Water Resources (DoWR), complementing existing structures and enhancing service delivery.ltbrgtIn Jebel Samaan, ACF will rehabilitate and solarise Al-Shorta PHC, serving over 40,000 people. The rehabilitation will include the provision of essential medicines, medical equipment, and operational support to ensure functionality in line with national protocols. Simultaneously, ACF will strengthen community-based health and nutrition services by deploying trained Community Health Workers (CHWs) in the areas of Al-Mansourah, Khan Tuman, Khan Al Asal, and Kafr Dael. CHWs will conduct household-level MUAC screenings, Infant and Young Child Feeding (IYCF) counselling, and referrals to DoH-supported CMAM facilities. Households with malnourished children and pregnant and lactating women (PLWs) will receive tailored WASH kits to mitigate the underlying causes of malnutrition.ltbrgtIn Khan Al-Asal, Mansourah, and Kafr Dael, ACF will restore WASH infrastructure where networks and boreholes have been damaged by conflict and neglect. In Khan Al-Asal, the Forest borehole will be rehabilitated, a new elevated tank constructed, and a 600-meter transmission line installed to connect it to households. Additionally, two existing boreholes will be connected to the public electricity grid. In Mansourah, one borehole will be rehabilitated and linked to the grid, while the elevated tank will undergo structural repair and a booster pump added. In Kafr Dael, ACF will rehabilitate a non-functional borehole, install a booster pump, and conduct maintenance on the elevated tank and distribution network to enhance household-level access.ltbrgtFor the FSL component, ACF will target highly vulnerable populations in Kafr Dael and Khan Tuman to protect and restore livelihoods. The intervention prioritises two groups: female-headed HHs with unstable income, and small-scale livestock breeders who have resorted to extreme coping strategies. For the first, under envelope 2, ACF will support 50 female-headed HHs (250 individuals) through agri-business management and technical training, coupled with cash or in-kind grants to launch income-generating activities. For group two, under envelope 1, 300 small-scale livestock breeders (1,500 individuals) will receive climate-smart support, including training on sustainable livestock practices, fodder management, and hydroponic systems. Each beneficiary will receive fodder inputs for three months and hydroponic trays to promote resilience.ltbrgtIn Karnaz Sub-district, ACF will restore access to essential health services through the light rehabilitation and solarisation of the DoH-affiliated PHC in Jalma, serving a catchment population of 6,000 people. The PHC will receive medical equipment and medicines to ensure continuity of care. The nutrition response in Jalma is covered by other ACF funding for continuity of CMAM and IYCF support. For WASH, ACF will rehabilitate a 120m-deep borehole, install a solar energy system, and construct a 100m³ elevated tank. Spot repairs to the damaged network and replacement of degraded fittings will restore gravity-fed water supply to currently underserved areas, reaching over 6,000 people. ltbrgtACF will collaborate with authorities (DoH, DoWR, MoH) at national and sub-national levels to ensure coordination, technical endorsement, and operational integration. The action’s value lies in its area-based and system-strengthening approach that delivers cost-effective, locally owned solutions.lt/pgt
